item.content: {"url": "https://api.crossref.org/works?query=experimental+or+theoretical+models+showing+divergence+between+bipartite+OTOC+and+redundancy+of+accessible+information&rows=4&select=DOI%2Ctitle%2Cabstract%2CURL%2Cpublished", "scope": "Crossref bibliographic metadata and abstracts where supplied; not full papers", "excerpt": "[{\"DOI\": \"10.1088/1367-2630/ad77ee\", \"title\": [\"Bipartite OTOC in open quantum systems: information scrambling and irreversibility\"], \"abstract\": \"<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>\\n               <jats:p>The field of information scrambling has seen significant growth over the last decade, where the out-of-time-ordered correlator (OTOC) has emerged as a prominent tool to probe it. In this work, we use bipartite OTOC, a particular form of OTOC, to study information scrambling in the atom–field interaction models and the model of the Ising spin chain interacting with a tilted magnetic field. This is done considering the effects of open quantum systems. A relationship between information scrambling, using bipartite OTOC, and irreversibility, using entropy production, is probed under unitary dynamics. The equivalence of bipartite OTOC with operator entanglement is explicitly shown for the Ising model.</jats:p>\", \"URL\": \"https://doi.org/10.1088/1367-2630/ad77ee\", \"published\": {\"date-parts\": [[2024, 9, 1]]}}, {\"DOI\": \"10.1021/ja5082712.s001\", \"title\": [\"Resolving Apparent Conflicts between Theoretical and Experimental Models of Phosphate Monoester Hydrolysis\"], \"URL\": \"https://doi.org/10.1021/ja5082712.s001\"}, {\"DOI\": \"10.7717/peerj.3807/fig-3\", \"title\": [\"Figure 3: Redundancy analysis ordination biplot showing the relationship between environmental variables and location.\"], \"URL\": \"https://doi.org/10.7717/peerj.3807/fig-3\"}, {\"DOI\": \"10.7717/peerj.14377/supp-1\", \"title\": [\"Supplemental Information 1: Bipartite network plot showing plant-pollinator interactions in (A) 2019, the year between fire season treatment and (B) 2020, the year when fire season treatments were again applied.\"], \"URL\": \"https://doi.org/10.7717/peerj.14377/supp-1\"}]", "excerpt_truncated": false, "source_sha256": "2cc6f745e443874b041bc6cc467432cf8070ebd418a46120db6884eb119127da", "verification_required": true, "topic_domain": "scrambling_records", "evidence_role": "discovery", "host_tier": "discovery", "source_identity"…
